sections.title: Section A — common to Mathematics and Applied Mathematics (compulsory)

questions.topic: Algebra: Matrices, Determinants, Inverse and the Matrix Method
questions.sub_topic: Determinant of a lower triangular 3 × 3 matrix
questions.question: The value of \(\begin{vmatrix}3&0&0\\2&-1&0\\5&4&2\end{vmatrix}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(-6\)
Given: all entries above the diagonal are 0
Formula: determinant of a triangular matrix = product of the diagonal entries
Step 1: \(3 \times (-1) \times 2 = -6\)
Common mistake: \(6\) (A) drops the minus sign. \(4\) (C) adds the diagonal entries.
Key point: Expand along the first row to see why only the diagonal matters.

questions.topic: Calculus: Derivatives, Increasing/Decreasing Functions, Maxima and Minima
questions.sub_topic: sin x + cos x on [0, π/2]
questions.question:
For \(f(x) = \sin x + \cos x\), \(0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), consider the following statements:
(A) \(f\) is strictly increasing on \(\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
(B) The maximum value of \(f\) on the interval is \(\sqrt{2}\).
(C) \(f(0) = f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\)
(D) \(f\) has a local minimum at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: \(f'(x) = \cos x - \sin x > 0\) on \(\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\), so (A) holds. \(f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}\) is the largest value, so (B) holds. \(f(0) = 1 = f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so (C) holds.
Why not the others: (D) is false: \(f'\) changes from positive to negative at \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), so it is a local maximum. Options (B) and (D) include (D); (A) leaves out (C).
Key point: \(f'\) going from + to − marks a maximum.

questions.topic: Algebra: Matrices, Determinants, Inverse and the Matrix Method
questions.sub_topic: Determinant of the adjoint from A adj A = 5I
questions.question: \(A\) is a square matrix of order 3 with \(A(\text{adj}\,A) = 5I\). Then \(|\text{adj}\,A|\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(25\)
Given: \(A(\text{adj}\,A) = |A|\,I\), so \(|A| = 5\); \(n = 3\)
Formula: \(|\text{adj}\,A| = |A|^{n-1}\)
Step 1: \(5^{3-1} = 25\)
Common mistake: \(125\) (C) uses \(|A|^n\). \(5\) (A) stops at \(|A|\).
Key point: For order \(n\), \(|\text{adj}\,A| = |A|^{n-1}\).

questions.topic: Calculus: Derivatives, Increasing/Decreasing Functions, Maxima and Minima
questions.sub_topic: Second derivative of tan x at π/4
questions.question: If \(y = \tan x\), then \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(4\)
Given: \(y' = \sec^2 x\)
Formula: \(y'' = 2\sec x \cdot \sec x\tan x = 2\sec^2 x\tan x\)
Step 1: At \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\): \(\sec^2 x = 2\), \(\tan x = 1\)
Step 2: \(y'' = 2 \times 2 \times 1 = 4\)
Common mistake: \(2\) (A) is \(y'\) at \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). \(1\) (C) is \(y\) itself.
Key point: Differentiate \(\sec^2 x\) with the chain rule.

questions.sub_topic: Variance of a four-valued distribution
questions.question: \(X\) takes the values 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4. The variance of \(X\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(1\)
Given: \(E(X) = 0.1 + 0.4 + 0.9 + 1.6 = 3\)
Formula: \(\text{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2\)
Step 1: \(E(X^2) = 0.1 + 0.8 + 2.7 + 6.4 = 10\)
Step 2: \(\text{Var}(X) = 10 - 9 = 1\)
Common mistake: \(3\) (A) is the mean. \(10\) (B) is \(E(X^2)\) with the mean not subtracted.
Key point: Subtract the square of the mean.

questions.sub_topic: Definite integral of tan² x on [0, π/4]
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^2 x\,dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(1 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
Given: \(\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1\)
Formula: \(\int(\sec^2 x - 1)\,dx = \tan x - x\)
Step 1: \(\left[\tan x - x\right]_0^{\pi/4} = 1 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
Common mistake: (D) uses \(\sec^2 x + 1\). (B) subtracts the limits the wrong way round.
Key point: Rewrite \(\tan^2 x\) before integrating.

questions.sub_topic: Maximum of x + y on a four-cornered region — which claims fail
questions.question:
For \(Z = x + y\) subject to \(x + 2y \le 8\), \(3x + 2y \le 12\), \(x, y \ge 0\), consider the following statements:
(A) The feasible region is bounded.
(B) The maximum value of \(Z\) is 4.
(C) \(Z = 4\) at two corner points.
(D) \((2, 3)\) is a corner point of the feasible region.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B) only
Why: Corners \((0, 0)\), \((4, 0)\), \((2, 3)\), \((0, 4)\) give \(Z = 0, 4, 5, 4\). Only (B) is false: the maximum is 5, at \((2, 3)\).
Why not the others: (A) both constraints keep \(x\) and \(y\) small. (C) at \((4, 0)\) and \((0, 4)\). (D) \(x + 2y = 8\) and \(3x + 2y = 12\) meet where \(2x = 4\), at \((2, 3)\). Options (A), (C) and (D) name a true statement as false.
Key point: Check the corner where two constraint lines cross.

questions.sub_topic: Separable equation with (y + 1) cos x
questions.question: The solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (y + 1)\cos x\) with \(y(0) = 0\) gives \(y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\) equal to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(e - 1\)
Given: \(\dfrac{dy}{y + 1} = \cos x\,dx\)
Formula: \(\log|y + 1| = \sin x + c\)
Step 1: \(y(0) = 0\): \(\log 1 = 0 + c\), so \(c = 0\) and \(y = e^{\sin x} - 1\)
Step 2: At \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\): \(y = e^1 - 1 = e - 1\)
Common mistake: \(e\) (B) forgets to subtract 1. \(1\) (D) stops at \(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
Key point: Solve for \(y\) after removing the log.

questions.sub_topic: Variance of the number of red balls drawn
questions.question: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement, and \(X\) is the number of red balls drawn. The variance of \(X\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(0.36\)
Given: \(P(X = 0) = \dfrac{1}{10}\), \(P(X = 1) = \dfrac{3 \times 2}{10} = \dfrac{6}{10}\), \(P(X = 2) = \dfrac{3}{10}\) (there are \(\binom{5}{2} = 10\) pairs)
Formula: \(\text{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2\)
Step 1: \(E(X) = 0.6 + 0.6 = 1.2\); \(E(X^2) = 0.6 + 1.2 = 1.8\)
Step 2: \(\text{Var}(X) = 1.8 - 1.44 = 0.36\)
Common mistake: \(0.48\) (D) uses the binomial \(npq = 2(0.6)(0.4)\), which needs drawing with replacement. \(1.2\) (A) is the mean.
Key point: Without replacement the draws are not independent, so build the distribution first.

questions.topic: Calculus: Derivatives, Increasing/Decreasing Functions, Maxima and Minima
questions.sub_topic: Open box from an 8 cm by 3 cm sheet
questions.question: Equal squares of side \(x\) cm are cut from the corners of a rectangular sheet 8 cm by 3 cm, and the sides are folded up to form an open box. The largest possible volume of the box is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(\dfrac{200}{27}\) cm³
Given: \(V = x(8 - 2x)(3 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 22x^2 + 24x\), \(0 < x < \dfrac{3}{2}\)
Formula: \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 44x + 24 = 4(3x - 2)(x - 3)\)
Step 1: \(V' = 0\) at \(x = \dfrac{2}{3}\) (\(x = 3\) is too big); \(V''\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 16 - 44 < 0\), a maximum
Step 2: \(V = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{20}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{200}{27}\)
Common mistake: \(6\) (A) tries \(x = 1\) instead of solving \(V' = 0\). (B) doubles the answer.
Key point: Reject critical points outside the allowed range of \(x\).

questions.topic: Algebra: Matrices, Determinants, Inverse and the Matrix Method
questions.sub_topic: Inverse of a matrix whose square is I
questions.question: For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&-2\end{bmatrix}\), \(A^{-1}\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&-2\end{bmatrix}\)
Given: \(|A| = -4 + 3 = -1\)
Formula: \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\text{adj}\,A\), with \(\text{adj}\,A = \begin{bmatrix}-2&1\\-3&2\end{bmatrix}\)
Step 1: Dividing by \(-1\) gives \(\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&-2\end{bmatrix} = A\)
Step 2: Check: \(A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}4 - 3&-2 + 2\\6 - 6&-3 + 4\end{bmatrix} = I\) ✓
Common mistake: (A) is the adjoint, not yet divided by \(|A| = -1\). (B) is the transpose.
Key point: If \(A^2 = I\), then \(A^{-1} = A\).

questions.sub_topic: Integral of cos 3x
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int\cos 3x\,dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x + C\)
Given: \(\int\cos ax\,dx\) with \(a = 3\)
Formula: \(\int\cos ax\,dx = \dfrac{1}{a}\sin ax + C\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x + C\)
Common mistake: (A) multiplies by 3, as in differentiation. (B) gives \(\cos\) the sign that belongs to \(\int\sin\).
Key point: Differentiate the answer to check it.

questions.topic: Algebra: Matrices, Determinants, Inverse and the Matrix Method
questions.sub_topic: Fifth power of I + N with N² = O
questions.question: For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}3&-4\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}\), \(A^5\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(\begin{bmatrix}11&-20\\5&-9\end{bmatrix}\)
Given: \(A = I + N\) with \(N = \begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}\)
Formula: \(N^2 = \begin{bmatrix}4 - 4&-8 + 8\\2 - 2&-4 + 4\end{bmatrix} = O\), so \((I + N)^n = I + nN\)
Step 1: \(A^5 = I + 5N = \begin{bmatrix}1 + 10&-20\\5&1 - 10\end{bmatrix}\)
Step 2: \(= \begin{bmatrix}11&-20\\5&-9\end{bmatrix}\)
Common mistake: (B) is \(5A\). (D) raises each entry to the fifth power, which is not how matrix powers work.
Key point: \(I\) commutes with every matrix, so the binomial expansion stops once \(N^2 = O\).

questions.sub_topic: Area between y = x² and y = 6 − x
questions.question: The area of the region enclosed by \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 6 - x\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(\dfrac{125}{6}\)
Given: \(x^2 = 6 - x \Rightarrow (x + 3)(x - 2) = 0\), so \(x = -3, 2\)
Formula: \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{2}(6 - x - x^2)\,dx = \left[6x - \dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^{2}\)
Step 1: At 2: \(12 - 2 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{22}{3}\)
Step 2: At \(-3\): \(-18 - \dfrac{9}{2} + 9 = -\dfrac{27}{2}\); area \(= \dfrac{22}{3} + \dfrac{27}{2} = \dfrac{125}{6}\)
Common mistake: (A) integrates only from 0 to 2. (B) integrates only from \(-3\) to 0.
Key point: Integrate (upper − lower) between the two meeting points.

questions.sub_topic: Values at x = 1 of four solutions through (0, 1)
questions.question:
Each differential equation in List-I is solved with \(y(0) = 1\). Match it with the value of \(y(1)\) in List-II.

List-I
(A) \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\)
(B) \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\)
(C) \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2y\)
(D) \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = xy\)

List-II
(I) \(1 + \log 2\)
(II) \(\sqrt{e}\)
(III) \(e\)
(IV) \(e^{-2}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Step 1: \(y = e^x\), so \(y(1) = e\) (III)
Step 2: \(y = \log(x + 1) + 1\), so \(y(1) = 1 + \log 2\) (I)
Step 3: \(y = e^{-2x}\), so \(y(1) = e^{-2}\) (IV)
Step 4: \(\dfrac{dy}{y} = x\,dx\) gives \(y = e^{x^2/2}\), so \(y(1) = \sqrt{e}\) (II)
Common mistake: In (D), forgetting the \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) in \(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\) gives \(e\), the value for (A).
Key point: Use \(y(0) = 1\) to fix the constant each time.

questions.sub_topic: Events with P(A ∪ B) = 0.7 — which claims fail
questions.question:
\(P(A) = 0.5\), \(P(B) = 0.4\) and \(P(A \cup B) = 0.7\). Consider the following statements:
(A) \(P(A \cap B) = 0.2\)
(B) \(A\) and \(B\) are mutually exclusive.
(C) \(A\) and \(B\) are independent.
(D) \(P(B \mid A) = 0.4\)
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B) only
Why: \(P(A \cap B) = 0.5 + 0.4 - 0.7 = 0.2\), so (A) holds. Only (B) is false: mutually exclusive needs \(P(A \cap B) = 0\).
Why not the others: (C) \(0.5 \times 0.4 = 0.2\). (D) \(\dfrac{0.2}{0.5} = 0.4\). Options (A), (B) and (C) name a true statement as false.
Key point: Independent and mutually exclusive are different; events with non-zero probabilities cannot be both.

questions.sub_topic: Where (x − 1)eˣ increases
questions.question: The function \(f(x) = (x - 1)e^x\) is strictly increasing on:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \((0, \infty)\)
Given: \(f'(x) = e^x + (x - 1)e^x = xe^x\)
Formula: \(e^x > 0\), so the sign of \(f'\) is that of \(x\)
Step 1: \(f'(x) > 0\) for \(x > 0\)
Common mistake: (C) uses the zero of \(f\), \(x = 1\), instead of the zero of \(f'\).
Key point: Monotonicity depends on \(f'\), not on \(f\).

questions.sub_topic: Product of the determinants of A⁻¹ and adj A
questions.question: \(A\) is a square matrix of order 3 with \(|A| = -2\). Then \(|A^{-1}| \cdot |\text{adj}\,A|\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(-2\)
Given: \(n = 3\), \(|A| = -2\)
Formula: \(|A^{-1}| = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\), \(|\text{adj}\,A| = |A|^{n-1}\)
Step 1: \(|A^{-1}| = -\dfrac{1}{2}\); \(|\text{adj}\,A| = (-2)^2 = 4\)
Step 2: Product \(= -\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 = -2\)
Common mistake: \(4\) (D) uses \(|\text{adj}\,A| = |A|^3 = -8\). \(2\) (B) drops the sign of \(|A^{-1}|\).
Key point: The product equals \(|A|^{n-2}\).

questions.sub_topic: Determinant with columns 1, a and b + c
questions.question: The value of \(\begin{vmatrix}1&a&b + c\\1&b&c + a\\1&c&a + b\end{vmatrix}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(0\)
Given: \(C_2 \to C_2 + C_3\) does not change the determinant
Formula: the new second column is \(a + b + c\) in every row
Step 1: Taking out \(a + b + c\) leaves two identical columns of 1s
Step 2: So the determinant is \(0\)
Common mistake: (D) is the value of the determinant with columns 1, \(a\), \(a^2\), a different pattern.
Key point: Look for a column operation that makes two columns proportional.

questions.topic: Unit III: Applications of the Integrals
questions.sub_topic: Area between y = sin x and the x-axis over [0, 2π]
questions.question: The area of the region bounded by \(y = \sin x\) and the \(x\)-axis between \(x = 0\) and \(x = 2\pi\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(4\)
Given: \(\sin x \ge 0\) on \([0, \pi]\) and \(\le 0\) on \([\pi, 2\pi]\)
Formula: area \(= \int_0^{\pi}\sin x\,dx + \left|\int_{\pi}^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx\right|\)
Step 1: \(2 + |-2| = 4\)
Common mistake: \(0\) (A) integrates straight across, so the two halves cancel. \(2\) (B) counts one arch.
Key point: Area below the axis is counted as positive.

questions.sub_topic: Derivative of log cos x
questions.question: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\log(\cos x)\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(-\tan x\)
Given: chain rule
Formula: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\log u = \dfrac{u'}{u}\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x} = -\tan x\)
Common mistake: \(\tan x\) (A) forgets that the derivative of \(\cos x\) is \(-\sin x\). (B) skips the chain rule.
Key point: Multiply by the derivative of the inside.

questions.sub_topic: Integral of x sec² x by parts
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int x\sec^2 x\,dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(x\tan x + \log|\cos x| + C\)
Given: \(u = x\), \(dv = \sec^2 x\,dx\), so \(v = \tan x\)
Formula: \(\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du\)
Step 1: \(x\tan x - \int\tan x\,dx\)
Step 2: \(\int\tan x\,dx = -\log|\cos x|\), so the answer is \(x\tan x + \log|\cos x| + C\)
Common mistake: (A) takes \(\int\tan x\,dx = \log|\cos x|\), with the wrong sign.
Key point: \(\int\tan x\,dx = \log|\sec x| = -\log|\cos x|\).

questions.sub_topic: Integral of sec x tan x
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int\sec x\tan x\,dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(\sec x + C\)
Given: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\sec x = \sec x\tan x\)
Formula: integration reverses differentiation
Step 1: \(\int\sec x\tan x\,dx = \sec x + C\)
Common mistake: (D) is \(\int\tan x\,dx\). (B) gives \(\sec x\) the sign of the \(\csc x\cot x\) result.
Key point: Learn each derivative together with its integral.

questions.sub_topic: Value of k making a root expression continuous
questions.question: \(f(x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + kx} - \sqrt{1 - kx}}{x}\) for \(-1 \le x < 0\), and \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 2}\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\). If \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 0\), then \(k\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\)
Given: \(f(0) = \dfrac{1}{-2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)
Formula: multiply by the conjugate: \(\dfrac{(1 + kx) - (1 - kx)}{x(\sqrt{1 + kx} + \sqrt{1 - kx})} = \dfrac{2k}{\sqrt{1 + kx} + \sqrt{1 - kx}}\)
Step 1: As \(x \to 0^-\), this tends to \(\dfrac{2k}{2} = k\)
Step 2: Continuity: \(k = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)
Common mistake: \(-\dfrac{1}{4}\) (D) forgets that the denominator tends to 2, not 1. (B) loses the sign of \(f(0)\).
Key point: Rationalise to remove the \(\dfrac{0}{0}\) form.

questions.sub_topic: The function x times the modulus of x — which claims fail
questions.question:
For \(f(x) = x|x|\), consider the following statements:
(A) \(f''(0)\) exists.
(B) \(f\) is continuous on \(\mathbb{R}\).
(C) \(f\) is differentiable at \(x = 0\).
(D) \(f'(x) = 2|x|\) for all real \(x\).
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A) only
Why: Only (A) is false. \(f(x) = x^2\) for \(x \ge 0\) and \(-x^2\) for \(x < 0\), so \(f'(x) = 2|x|\), whose graph has a corner at 0; hence \(f''(0)\) does not exist.
Why not the others: (B) both pieces are 0 at \(x = 0\). (C) \(\dfrac{f(h) - f(0)}{h} = |h| \to 0\). (D) \(2x\) for \(x \ge 0\), \(-2x\) for \(x < 0\). Options (A), (B) and (C) name a true statement as false.
Key point: \(f\) can be differentiable while \(f'\) is not.

questions.sub_topic: Rate at which a shadow lengthens
questions.question: A man 2 m tall walks away from a lamp post 6 m high at 5 km/h. The rate at which the length of his shadow increases is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(\dfrac{5}{2}\) km/h
Given: distance from the post \(x\), shadow length \(s\), \(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 5\)
Formula: similar triangles: \(\dfrac{s}{2} = \dfrac{x + s}{6}\), so \(6s = 2x + 2s\) and \(s = \dfrac{x}{2}\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 = \dfrac{5}{2}\) km/h
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{15}{2}\) (D) is the speed of the tip of the shadow, \(\dfrac{d(x + s)}{dt}\).
Key point: Relate \(s\) to \(x\) first, then differentiate.

questions.sub_topic: Parallelogram on 2a + b and a − b
questions.question: \(|\vec{a}| = 2\), \(|\vec{b}| = 3\) and the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides \(2\vec{a} + \vec{b}\) and \(\vec{a} - \vec{b}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(9\sqrt{3}\)
Given: \(\vec{a} \times \vec{a} = \vec{b} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}\), \(\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = -\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\)
Formula: \((2\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} - \vec{b}) = -2\vec{a} \times \vec{b} + \vec{b} \times \vec{a} = -3\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\)
Step 1: \(|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = 2 \times 3 \times \sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = 3\sqrt{3}\)
Step 2: Area \(= 3 \times 3\sqrt{3} = 9\sqrt{3}\)
Common mistake: \(3\sqrt{3}\) (B) treats \(\vec{b} \times \vec{a}\) as \(+\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\), so \(-2 + 1 = -1\). (D) uses \(\cos\) in place of \(\sin\).
Key point: Expand the cross product term by term, minding the order.

questions.sub_topic: A pair related to (2, 5) when a + d = b + c
questions.question: On \(\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}\), \((a, b)\,R\,(c, d)\) means \(a + d = b + c\). Which pair is related to \((2, 5)\)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \((1, 4)\)
Given: \((2, 5)\,R\,(c, d)\) needs \(2 + d = 5 + c\), that is \(d - c = 3\)
Formula: test each pair
Step 1: \((1, 4)\): \(4 - 1 = 3\) ✓
Step 2: \((5, 2)\) and \((4, 1)\) give \(-3\); \((3, 5)\) gives 2
Common mistake: (A) reverses the pair; the relation compares \(b - a\), not just the numbers.
Key point: \(a + d = b + c\) means \(b - a = d - c\).

questions.sub_topic: Recovering A from 3A − B
questions.question: If \(3A - B = \begin{bmatrix}5&0\\1&1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix}4&3\\2&5\end{bmatrix}\), then \(A\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\)
Given: \(3A = \begin{bmatrix}5&0\\1&1\end{bmatrix} + B\)
Formula: \(3A = \begin{bmatrix}9&3\\3&6\end{bmatrix}\)
Step 1: \(A = \dfrac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}9&3\\3&6\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}3&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\)
Common mistake: (A) subtracts \(B\) instead of adding it. (B) forgets to divide by 3.
Key point: Move \(B\) across with the opposite sign.

questions.sub_topic: Principal values after reducing the angle
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) \(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)\)
(B) \(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\)
(C) \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\)
(D) \(\cot^{-1}(-1)\)

List-II
(I) \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\)
(II) \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\)
(III) \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\)
(IV) \(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Step 1: \(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), and \(\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\) (II)
Step 2: \(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\), and \(\tan^{-1}(-1) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) (IV)
Step 3: \(\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), and \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) (I)
Step 4: \(\cot^{-1}\) has range \((0, \pi)\), and \(\cot\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\) (III)
Common mistake: Writing \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) for (B) by cancelling \(\tan^{-1}\) with \(\tan\); \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) lies outside \(\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
Key point: Find the value inside first, then take the principal value.

questions.sub_topic: Angle between lines with ratios 3, −6, 2 and 2, 1, 2
questions.question: The angle between two lines with direction ratios \(3, -6, 2\) and \(2, 1, 2\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(\cos^{-1}\dfrac{4}{21}\)
Given: \(\sqrt{9 + 36 + 4} = 7\), \(\sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3\)
Formula: \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{|a_1a_2 + b_1b_2 + c_1c_2|}{\sqrt{\ldots}\sqrt{\ldots}}\)
Step 1: \(6 - 6 + 4 = 4\)
Step 2: \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{21}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{16}{21}\) (D) takes \(b_1b_2 = +6\). (A) divides by 7 only.
Key point: Divide by both magnitudes.

questions.sub_topic: Rules of matrix algebra that always hold
questions.question:
For square matrices \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) of the same order and a scalar \(k\), consider the following statements:
(A) \(AB = BA\)
(B) \((A + B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2\)
(C) \(A(B + C) = AB + AC\)
(D) \((kA)B = k(AB)\)
Which of the statements given above are correct for all such matrices?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C) and (D) only
Why: (C) is the distributive law and (D) lets a scalar move freely; both always hold.
Why not the others: (A) fails, e.g. \(\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{bmatrix} \ne \begin{bmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\). (B) fails because \((A + B)^2 = A^2 + AB + BA + B^2\). Options (A), (C) and (D) include (A) or (B).
Key point: Matrix multiplication is not commutative.

questions.sub_topic: Linear equation y′ + y/x = x²
questions.question: The general solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = x^2\) (\(x > 0\)) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(y = \dfrac{x^3}{4} + \dfrac{C}{x}\)
Given: \(P = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(Q = x^2\)
Formula: I.F. \(= e^{\int dx/x} = x\)
Step 1: \(xy = \int x^3\,dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4} + C\)
Step 2: \(y = \dfrac{x^3}{4} + \dfrac{C}{x}\)
Common mistake: (A) integrates \(x^2\) instead of \(x \cdot x^2\). (D) forgets to divide by the I.F.
Key point: Multiply \(Q\) by the I.F. before integrating.

questions.sub_topic: Minimum of −3x + 4y on a bounded region
questions.question: The minimum value of \(Z = -3x + 4y\) subject to \(x + 2y \le 10\), \(2x + y \le 8\), \(x, y \ge 0\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(-12\)
Given: corners \((0, 0)\), \((4, 0)\), \((2, 4)\), \((0, 5)\)
Formula: evaluate \(Z\) at each corner
Step 1: \(Z = 0, -12, 10, 20\)
Step 2: The minimum is \(-12\), at \((4, 0)\)
Common mistake: \(0\) (B) assumes the origin always gives the minimum; that fails when a coefficient is negative. \(20\) (D) is the maximum.
Key point: Find \((2, 4)\) by solving \(x + 2y = 10\) and \(2x + y = 8\).

questions.sub_topic: Simplifying sin⁻¹(cos 3π/5)
questions.question: \(\sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{5}\right)\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(-\dfrac{\pi}{10}\)
Given: \(\cos\theta = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)\)
Formula: \(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{5} = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{3\pi}{5}\right) = \sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{10}\right)\)
Step 1: \(-\dfrac{\pi}{10}\) lies in \(\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\)
Step 2: So \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{10}\right)\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{10}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{\pi}{10}\) (B) loses the sign; \(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{5}\) is negative. (C) cancels \(\sin^{-1}\) against \(\cos\).
Key point: Convert to the same function, then check the principal range.

questions.sub_topic: At least two heads, given the first coin is a head
questions.question: Three fair coins are tossed. Given that the first coin shows a head, the probability of at least two heads is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(\dfrac{3}{4}\)
Given: \(F\) = first is a head = {HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT}
Formula: \(P(E \mid F) = \dfrac{n(E \cap F)}{n(F)}\)
Step 1: \(E \cap F\) = {HHH, HHT, HTH}
Step 2: \(P(E \mid F) = \dfrac{3}{4}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{3}{8}\) (C) is \(P(E \cap F)\). \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) (A) is \(P(E)\), ignoring the condition.
Key point: The condition shrinks the sample space.

questions.sub_topic: Bayes' theorem: a lost card was a diamond
questions.question: One card is lost from a well-shuffled pack of 52. Two cards are then drawn from the remaining 51 and both are diamonds. The probability that the lost card was a diamond is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(\dfrac{11}{50}\)
Given: \(P(E_1) = \dfrac{1}{4}\) (lost card a diamond), \(P(E_2) = \dfrac{3}{4}\)
Formula: \(P(A \mid E_1) = \dfrac{\binom{12}{2}}{\binom{51}{2}}\), \(P(A \mid E_2) = \dfrac{\binom{13}{2}}{\binom{51}{2}}\)
Step 1: \(P(E_1 \mid A) = \dfrac{\frac{1}{4} \times 66}{\frac{1}{4} \times 66 + \frac{3}{4} \times 78}\)
Step 2: \(= \dfrac{66}{66 + 234} = \dfrac{66}{300} = \dfrac{11}{50}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) (A) is the prior and ignores the evidence. \(\dfrac{13}{50}\) (D) uses 13 diamonds left in the first case.
Key point: The common factor \(\binom{51}{2}\) cancels.

questions.sub_topic: Four facts about one line in vector form
questions.question:
For the line \(\vec{r} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) + \lambda(2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\), match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) The point on the line with \(\lambda = 1\)
(B) Its direction cosines
(C) The angle it makes with the \(z\)-axis
(D) Its Cartesian equation

List-II
(I) \((3, 1, 2)\)
(II) \(\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{2}\)
(III) \(\dfrac{2}{3}, -\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{2}{3}\)
(IV) \(\cos^{-1}\dfrac{2}{3}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Step 1: \(\lambda = 1\): \((1 + 2, 2 - 1, 0 + 2) = (3, 1, 2)\) (I)
Step 2: \(|2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}| = 3\), so the direction cosines are \(\dfrac{2}{3}, -\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{2}{3}\) (III)
Step 3: \(\cos\gamma = n = \dfrac{2}{3}\) (IV)
Step 4: Through \((1, 2, 0)\) with ratios \(2, -1, 2\) (II)
Common mistake: Writing \(\dfrac{z - 2}{2}\) in (D); the point \(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\) has \(z = 0\).
Key point: The direction cosine \(n\) is the cosine of the angle with the \(z\)-axis.

questions.sub_topic: Angle between i + j − k and i − j + k
questions.question: The angle between \(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\)
Given: \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1 - 1 - 1 = -1\); \(|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = \sqrt{3}\)
Formula: \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|}\)
Step 1: \(\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\)
Common mistake: (A) loses the sign of the dot product. (D) divides by \(\sqrt{3}\) only once.
Key point: A negative dot product means an obtuse angle.

questions.sub_topic: Is x² a bijection on R?
questions.question: The function \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x^2\), is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) neither one-one nor onto
Why: \(f(-1) = f(1) = 1\), so \(f\) is not one-one; no real \(x\) gives \(f(x) = -1\), so it is not onto.
Why not the others: (B) and (D) need one-one. (C) and (D) need every real number, including negatives, to be a value.
Key point: Check both properties separately.

questions.sub_topic: Is x/(x + 1) onto R?
questions.question: The function \(f: \mathbb{R} - \{-1\} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x + 1}\), is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) one-one but not onto
Why: \(f(x) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\). If \(f(a) = f(b)\), then \(\dfrac{1}{a + 1} = \dfrac{1}{b + 1}\), so \(a = b\): one-one. \(f(x) = 1\) would need \(\dfrac{1}{x + 1} = 0\), which never happens, so 1 is not a value.
Why not the others: (A), (C) need onto, but the range is \(\mathbb{R} - \{1\}\). (D) ignores that \(f\) is one-one.
Key point: Solve \(y = f(x)\) for \(x\) to find which \(y\) are missed.

questions.sub_topic: Maximum value of (1/x)ˣ
questions.question: For \(x > 0\), the maximum value of \(f(x) = \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^x\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(e^{1/e}\)
Given: \(\log f = -x\log x\)
Formula: \(\dfrac{f'}{f} = -(\log x + 1)\)
Step 1: \(f' = 0\) at \(\log x = -1\), i.e. \(x = \dfrac{1}{e}\); \(f'\) changes from + to −, a maximum
Step 2: \(f\left(\dfrac{1}{e}\right) = e^{1/e}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{1}{e}\) (B) is the point, not the value. (D) evaluates at \(x = e\).
Key point: Take logs before differentiating a variable power.

questions.sub_topic: Parametric slope for eᵗ cos t and eᵗ sin t
questions.question: If \(x = e^t\cos t\) and \(y = e^t\sin t\), then \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) at \(t = 0\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(1\)
Given: \(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = e^t(\cos t - \sin t)\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dt} = e^t(\sin t + \cos t)\)
Formula: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sin t + \cos t}{\cos t - \sin t}\)
Step 1: At \(t = 0\): \(\dfrac{0 + 1}{1 - 0} = 1\)
Common mistake: \(0\) (A) differentiates \(\sin t\) alone and forgets the product rule.
Key point: The \(e^t\) factors cancel.

questions.sub_topic: Homogeneous equation with a square root
questions.question: The general solution of \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) (\(x > 0\)) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = Cx^2\)
Given: \(y = vx\), \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\)
Formula: \(x\left(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) - vx = x\sqrt{1 + v^2}\), so \(\dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1 + v^2}} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\)
Step 1: \(\log\left|v + \sqrt{1 + v^2}\right| = \log x + \log C\)
Step 2: \(\dfrac{y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x} = Cx\), so \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = Cx^2\)
Common mistake: (B) forgets to multiply back by \(x\) when replacing \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\).
Key point: After substituting back, clear the \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) carefully.

questions.sub_topic: Order for the family of circles centred at the origin
questions.question: The order of the differential equation of the family of circles \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\) (\(r\) arbitrary) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(1\)
Given: one arbitrary constant, \(r\)
Formula: order = number of arbitrary constants to eliminate
Step 1: \(2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\), i.e. \(x + y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\): order 1
Common mistake: \(2\) (A) counts the two variables \(x\) and \(y\) instead of the constants.
Key point: Differentiate once for each arbitrary constant.

questions.sub_topic: Integral of a sum of three moduli on [1, 4]
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int_1^4\left(|x - 1| + |x - 2| + |x - 3|\right)dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(\dfrac{19}{2}\)
Given: split each modulus at its zero
Formula: \(\int_1^4|x - 1|\,dx = \dfrac{9}{2}\)
Step 1: \(\int_1^4|x - 2|\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 = \dfrac{5}{2}\)
Step 2: \(\int_1^4|x - 3|\,dx = 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}\); total \(= \dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{19}{2}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{9}{2}\) (B) drops the modulus signs and integrates \(3x - 6\).
Key point: Each modulus is a triangle area on either side of its zero.

questions.sub_topic: Shortest distance between two skew lines with a = (3, 3, 3)
questions.question: The shortest distance between \(\vec{r} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\) and \(\vec{r} = (4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}) + \mu(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \hat{k})\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{19}}\)
Given: \(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1 = 3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\)
Formula: \(d = \dfrac{|(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1)\cdot(\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)|}{|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2|}\)
Step 1: \(\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 = (-3 - 6)\hat{i} - (1 - 4)\hat{j} + (3 + 6)\hat{k} = -9\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 9\hat{k}\), magnitude \(\sqrt{171} = 3\sqrt{19}\)
Step 2: Dot product: \(-27 + 9 + 27 = 9\); \(d = \dfrac{9}{3\sqrt{19}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{19}}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{19}}\) (D) divides by \(\sqrt{19}\) instead of \(3\sqrt{19}\).
Key point: Simplify \(\sqrt{171} = 3\sqrt{19}\) before dividing.

questions.sub_topic: Facts about cross and dot products
questions.question:
For vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\), consider the following statements:
(A) \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = -(\vec{b} \times \vec{a})\)
(B) \(\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{k}\)
(C) \(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = 0\)
(D) \(|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 + (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})^2 = |\vec{a}|^2|\vec{b}|^2\)
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: (A) the cross product changes sign when the order is reversed. (C) \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{a}\). (D) \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) times \(|\vec{a}|^2|\vec{b}|^2\).
Why not the others: (B) is false: \(\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}\). Options (B) and (D) include (B); (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: \(\hat{i} \to \hat{j} \to \hat{k}\) in cyclic order gives a positive cross product.

questions.sub_topic: An entry of a 3 × 3 inverse from one cofactor
questions.question: For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1&-1&2\\0&2&-3\\3&-2&4\end{bmatrix}\), the entry in row 2, column 1 of \(A^{-1}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(9\)
Given: \(|A| = 1(8 - 6) + 1(0 + 9) + 2(0 - 6) = -1\)
Formula: \((A^{-1})_{21} = \dfrac{(\text{adj}\,A)_{21}}{|A|} = \dfrac{C_{12}}{|A|}\), because the adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix
Step 1: \(C_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix}0&-3\\3&4\end{vmatrix} = -(0 + 9) = -9\)
Step 2: \((A^{-1})_{21} = \dfrac{-9}{-1} = 9\)
Common mistake: \(0\) (C) uses \(C_{21}\), forgetting the transpose. \(-9\) (A) forgets to divide by \(|A| = -1\).
Key point: Row 2, column 1 of \(A^{-1}\) uses the cofactor of row 1, column 2.

questions.sub_topic: Four standard integrals with a = 2
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II (constants omitted).

List-I
(A) \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2 - 4}\)
(B) \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 - 4}}\)
(C) \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{4 - x^2}\)
(D) \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}\)

List-II
(I) \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\)
(II) \(\dfrac{1}{4}\log\left|\dfrac{2 + x}{2 - x}\right|\)
(III) \(\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2 - 4}\right|\)
(IV) \(\dfrac{1}{4}\log\left|\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 2}\right|\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Step 1: \(\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2 - a^2} = \dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{x - a}{x + a}\right|\) (IV)
Step 2: \(\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} = \log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2 - a^2}\right|\) (III)
Step 3: \(\int\dfrac{dx}{a^2 - x^2} = \dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{a + x}{a - x}\right|\) (II)
Step 4: \(\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}} = \sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\) (I)
Common mistake: Swapping (A) and (C); the two log forms differ in the order \(x - a\) versus \(a + x\).
Key point: With \(a = 2\), \(\dfrac{1}{2a} = \dfrac{1}{4}\).

questions.sub_topic: Derivative of 3x² − log x
questions.question: If \(y = 3x^2 - \log x\) (\(x > 0\)), then \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(6x - \dfrac{1}{x}\)
Given: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}x^2 = 2x\), \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\log x = \dfrac{1}{x}\)
Formula: differentiate term by term
Step 1: \(6x - \dfrac{1}{x}\)
Common mistake: (B) loses the minus sign. (D) leaves \(\log x\) undifferentiated.
Key point: Keep each term's sign.

questions.sub_topic: Money split across three schemes
questions.question: ₹10,000 is invested in three schemes paying 5%, 6% and 8% simple interest a year. The total yearly interest is ₹590, and the amount in the 5% scheme equals the other two amounts together. The amount in the 8% scheme is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ₹2,000
Given: \(x + y + z = 10000\), \(0.05x + 0.06y + 0.08z = 590\), \(x = y + z\)
Formula: from the first and third, \(x = 5000\) and \(y + z = 5000\)
Step 1: \(0.06y + 0.08z = 590 - 250 = 340\), i.e. \(6y + 8z = 34000\)
Step 2: With \(y = 5000 - z\): \(30000 + 2z = 34000 \Rightarrow z = 2000\)
Common mistake: ₹3,000 (A) is the amount in the 6% scheme. ₹5,000 (C) is the 5% scheme.
Key point: Check: \(250 + 180 + 160 = 590\) ✓.

questions.sub_topic: t-statistic from five observations with μ₀ = 5
questions.question: A sample gives 2, 6, 8, 10, 14. To test \(H_0: \mu = 5\), the \(t\)-statistic is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(1.5\)
Given: \(\bar{x} = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8\); deviations \(-6, -2, 0, 2, 6\)
Formula: \(s^2 = \dfrac{\sum(x - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}\), \(t = \dfrac{\bar{x} - \mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}}\)
Step 1: \(\sum(x - \bar{x})^2 = 36 + 4 + 0 + 4 + 36 = 80\), \(s^2 = 20\)
Step 2: SE \(= \sqrt{\dfrac{20}{5}} = 2\); \(t = \dfrac{8 - 5}{2} = 1.5\)
Common mistake: \(1.68\) (C) divides by \(n = 5\) instead of \(n - 1 = 4\). \(3\) (A) forgets to divide by the SE.
Key point: Use \(n - 1\) for the sample variance in a t-test.

questions.sub_topic: Annual write-off for a machine with a ₹30,000 scrap value
questions.question: A machine costs ₹1,50,000, has a scrap value of ₹30,000 and a useful life of 8 years. The annual depreciation by the straight-line method is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹15,000
Given: cost ₹1,50,000, scrap ₹30,000, life 8 years
Formula: \(\dfrac{\text{cost} - \text{scrap}}{\text{life}}\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{1{,}20{,}000}{8} = ₹15{,}000\)
Common mistake: ₹18,750 (A) ignores the scrap value. ₹22,500 (C) adds the scrap value.
Key point: Only cost minus scrap is written off.

questions.sub_topic: Standard deviation of B(16, 1/4)
questions.question: For a binomial distribution with \(n = 16\) and \(p = \dfrac{1}{4}\), the standard deviation is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(\sqrt{3}\)
Given: \(q = \dfrac{3}{4}\)
Formula: SD \(= \sqrt{npq}\)
Step 1: \(\sqrt{16 \times \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{3}{4}} = \sqrt{3}\)
Common mistake: \(3\) (A) is the variance. \(4\) (B) is the mean.
Key point: Take the square root of the variance.

questions.sub_topic: Seven-year trend line, then a forecast
questions.question: Values for 2017–2023 were 10, 12, 11, 15, 16, 18, 23. Coding the years as \(x = -3, \ldots, 3\) (origin 2020) and fitting \(y = a + bx\) by least squares, the estimated value for 2025 is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(25\)
Given: \(\sum y = 105\), \(\sum x^2 = 9 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 4 + 9 = 28\)
Formula: \(a = \dfrac{\sum y}{n} = 15\), \(b = \dfrac{\sum xy}{\sum x^2}\)
Step 1: \(\sum xy = -30 - 24 - 11 + 0 + 16 + 36 + 69 = 56\), so \(b = 2\)
Step 2: 2025 has \(x = 5\): \(y = 15 + 2 \times 5 = 25\)
Common mistake: \(27\) (B) takes \(x = 6\), counting from 2019. \(23\) (A) repeats the last value.
Key point: Code 2025 from the same origin, 2020.

questions.sub_topic: Integral of x e^(x²)
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int xe^{x^2}\,dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(\dfrac{1}{2}e^{x^2} + C\)
Given: \(t = x^2\), \(dt = 2x\,dx\)
Formula: \(\dfrac{1}{2}\int e^t\,dt\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{1}{2}e^{x^2} + C\)
Common mistake: (C) multiplies by 2 instead of dividing. (A) forgets the factor.
Key point: Differentiate to check: \(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2xe^{x^2} = xe^{x^2}\) ✓.

questions.topic: Unit I: Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications
questions.sub_topic: A filling pipe and a slower pipe — which hold
questions.question:
Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B fills it in 12 hours. Consider the following statements:
(A) Working together, they fill the tank in 4 hours.
(B) Working together, they fill \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of the tank in one hour.
(C) If B is used as an outlet emptying at the same rate while A fills, the tank fills in 12 hours.
(D) B alone takes 3 hours to fill the tank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: Together \(\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{4}\) per hour, so (A) and (B) hold. With B emptying, \(\dfrac{1}{6} - \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{12}\) per hour, so (C) holds.
Why not the others: (D) is false: B takes 12 hours, as given. Options (C) and (D) include (D); (A) leaves out (C).
Key point: Add the rates of filling pipes and subtract the rates of emptying pipes.

questions.sub_topic: Expected net gain from a lottery ticket
questions.question: A lottery ticket costs ₹20. It wins a prize of ₹500 with probability 0.01 and a prize of ₹100 with probability 0.05; otherwise it wins nothing. The expected prize minus the cost of the ticket is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) −₹10
Given: prizes 500, 100, 0 with probabilities 0.01, 0.05, 0.94
Formula: \(E(\text{prize}) = \sum xP(x)\)
Step 1: \(500(0.01) + 100(0.05) = 5 + 5 = 10\)
Step 2: Net \(= 10 - 20 = -10\)
Common mistake: ₹10 (A) forgets the cost of the ticket. −₹20 (B) ignores the prizes.
Key point: A negative expected value means a loss on average.

questions.sub_topic: t-statistic from Σx and Σx² for a sample of 16
questions.question: A sample of 16 has \(\sum x = 880\) and \(\sum x^2 = 49360\). To test \(H_0: \mu = 51\), the \(t\)-statistic is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(2\)
Given: \(\bar{x} = \dfrac{880}{16} = 55\)
Formula: \(\sum(x - \bar{x})^2 = \sum x^2 - n\bar{x}^2\)
Step 1: \(49360 - 16 \times 3025 = 49360 - 48400 = 960\); \(s^2 = \dfrac{960}{15} = 64\), \(s = 8\)
Step 2: SE \(= \dfrac{8}{4} = 2\); \(t = \dfrac{55 - 51}{2} = 2\)
Common mistake: \(2.07\) (B) divides 960 by 16 instead of 15. \(0.5\) (C) divides by \(s\) rather than the SE.
Key point: Convert \(\sum x^2\) to the sum of squared deviations first.

questions.topic: Unit I: Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications
questions.sub_topic: Ratio for mixing rice at ₹30 and ₹45 to get ₹40
questions.question: In what ratio must rice costing ₹30 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹45 per kg to get a mixture worth ₹40 per kg?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(1 : 2\)
Given: cheaper ₹30, dearer ₹45, mean ₹40
Formula: cheaper : dearer \(= (45 - 40) : (40 - 30)\)
Step 1: \(5 : 10 = 1 : 2\)
Common mistake: \(2 : 1\) (A) reverses the ratio.
Key point: The mean is nearer the dearer price, so more of the dearer rice is used.

questions.sub_topic: Growth, perpetuities, depreciation and bonds — which claims fail
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) ₹1,000 growing to ₹1,210 in 2 years is a CAGR of 10%.
(B) The present value of a perpetuity of ₹1,200 a year at 6% is ₹7,200.
(C) The straight-line method charges the same depreciation every year.
(D) A bond priced above its face value has a yield below its coupon rate.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B) only
Why: Only (B) is false: the present value is \(\dfrac{1200}{0.06} = ₹20{,}000\); ₹7,200 multiplies instead of dividing.
Why not the others: (A) \(1000(1.1)^2 = 1210\). (C) \(\dfrac{\text{cost} - \text{scrap}}{\text{life}}\) is constant. (D) a buyer pays a premium only when the coupon exceeds the market yield. Options (A), (B) and (C) name a true statement as false.
Key point: Perpetuity present value \(= \dfrac{R}{i}\).

questions.sub_topic: Price that maximises profit
questions.question: The demand function is \(p = 200 - 4x\) and the cost function is \(C = x^2 + 20x + 100\) (in ₹). The price at which profit is greatest is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) ₹128
Given: \(R = px = 200x - 4x^2\)
Formula: \(P = R - C = 180x - 5x^2 - 100\); \(P' = 180 - 10x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 18\); \(P'' = -10 < 0\)
Step 1: Price \(p = 200 - 4 \times 18 = 128\)
Step 2: (Profit \(= 3240 - 1620 - 100 = 1520\), not asked)
Common mistake: ₹56 (A) is the common value of MR and MC at \(x = 18\). ₹1,520 (B) is the profit.
Key point: Find \(x\) first, then put it in the demand function.

questions.sub_topic: Normal probability below one SD under the mean
questions.question: \(X\) is normal with mean 40 and standard deviation 5. Given \(P(0 < Z < 1) = 0.3413\), \(P(X < 35)\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(0.1587\)
Given: \(Z = \dfrac{35 - 40}{5} = -1\)
Formula: \(P(Z < -1) = 0.5 - P(-1 < Z < 0)\)
Step 1: By symmetry \(P(-1 < Z < 0) = 0.3413\)
Step 2: \(P(Z < -1) = 0.5 - 0.3413 = 0.1587\)
Common mistake: \(0.8413\) (C) is \(P(Z < 1)\). \(0.3413\) (A) stops at the table value.
Key point: Each half of the normal curve has area 0.5.

questions.topic: Unit I: Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications
questions.sub_topic: Stream speed from a round trip and a time ratio
questions.question: A man rows to a place 48 km away and back in 14 hours. He can row 4 km downstream in the same time as 3 km upstream. The speed of the stream is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(1\) km/h
Given: downstream : upstream speed \(= 4 : 3\), say \(4k\) and \(3k\)
Formula: \(\dfrac{48}{4k} + \dfrac{48}{3k} = 14\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{12}{k} + \dfrac{16}{k} = 14 \Rightarrow k = 2\): downstream 8, upstream 6 km/h
Step 2: Stream \(= \dfrac{8 - 6}{2} = 1\) km/h
Common mistake: \(7\) km/h (C) is the speed in still water, \(\dfrac{8 + 6}{2}\).
Key point: Equal times mean the distances are in the ratio of the speeds.

questions.topic: Unit I: Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications
questions.sub_topic: Remainder of 2⁴⁰ on division by 7
questions.question: The remainder when \(2^{40}\) is divided by 7 is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(2\)
Given: \(2^3 = 8 \equiv 1 \pmod 7\)
Formula: \(2^{40} = (2^3)^{13} \times 2\)
Step 1: \(\equiv 1^{13} \times 2 = 2 \pmod 7\)
Common mistake: \(1\) (A) treats 40 as a multiple of 3. \(4\) (B) uses \(2^{40} = (2^3)^{13} \times 2^2\).
Key point: Find a power that is \(\equiv 1\) and split the exponent.

questions.sub_topic: Producer surplus at market equilibrium
questions.question: The demand function is \(p = 15 - x\) and the supply function is \(p = 3 + 2x\). The producer surplus at market equilibrium is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(16\)
Given: \(15 - x = 3 + 2x \Rightarrow x_0 = 4\), \(p_0 = 11\)
Formula: \(PS = p_0x_0 - \int_0^{x_0}(3 + 2x)\,dx\)
Step 1: \(\int_0^4(3 + 2x)\,dx = 12 + 16 = 28\)
Step 2: \(PS = 44 - 28 = 16\)
Common mistake: \(8\) (A) is the consumer surplus. \(28\) (B) stops at the integral.
Key point: Producer surplus is the area between the price line and the supply curve.

questions.sub_topic: Effective rate for 12% compounded monthly
questions.question: The effective annual rate equivalent to a nominal rate of 12% per annum compounded monthly is about:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(12.68\%\)
Given: \(i = 0.01\) per month, 12 periods
Formula: \(r_{\text{eff}} = (1 + i)^{12} - 1\)
Step 1: \((1.01)^{12} \approx 1.1268\)
Step 2: \(r_{\text{eff}} \approx 12.68\%\)
Common mistake: \(12.55\%\) (C) is for quarterly compounding and \(12.36\%\) (D) for half-yearly.
Key point: More frequent compounding gives a higher effective rate.

questions.sub_topic: Definite integral of √x on [1, 4]
questions.question: \(\displaystyle\int_1^4\sqrt{x}\,dx\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(\dfrac{14}{3}\)
Given: \(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\)
Formula: \(\int x^{1/2}\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\)
Step 1: \(\dfrac{2}{3}\left(4^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}(8 - 1) = \dfrac{14}{3}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{16}{3}\) (A) forgets the lower limit. \(\dfrac{7}{3}\) (C) uses \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) instead of \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).
Key point: \(4^{3/2} = (\sqrt{4})^3 = 8\).

questions.topic: Unit I: Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications
questions.sub_topic: Inequality with two moduli
questions.question: The solution set of \(|x - 1| + |x - 2| \ge 4\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(\left(-\infty, -\dfrac{1}{2}\right] \cup \left[\dfrac{7}{2}, \infty\right)\)
Given: the sum equals \(3 - 2x\) for \(x \le 1\), \(1\) for \(1 < x < 2\), \(2x - 3\) for \(x \ge 2\)
Formula: solve on each interval
Step 1: \(x \le 1\): \(3 - 2x \ge 4 \Rightarrow x \le -\dfrac{1}{2}\); \(1 < x < 2\): \(1 \ge 4\) is false
Step 2: \(x \ge 2\): \(2x - 3 \ge 4 \Rightarrow x \ge \dfrac{7}{2}\)
Common mistake: (B) solves \(\le 4\) instead. (C) just uses the points where the moduli change.
Key point: Split the line at each zero of a modulus.

questions.sub_topic: Exactly two doublets in four throws of two dice
questions.question: A pair of dice is thrown 4 times. Getting a doublet (both dice the same) is a success. The probability of exactly two successes is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(\dfrac{25}{216}\)
Given: \(p = \dfrac{6}{36} = \dfrac{1}{6}\), \(q = \dfrac{5}{6}\), \(n = 4\)
Formula: \(P(X = 2) = \binom{4}{2}p^2q^2\)
Step 1: \(6 \times \dfrac{1}{36} \times \dfrac{25}{36} = \dfrac{150}{1296}\)
Step 2: \(= \dfrac{25}{216}\)
Common mistake: \(\dfrac{25}{1296}\) (B) leaves out \(\binom{4}{2} = 6\). (D) uses 12 arrangements instead of 6.
Key point: There are 6 doublets among the 36 outcomes.

questions.sub_topic: How moving averages behave — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the moving-average method:
(A) A four-yearly moving average must be centred to line up with the years.
(B) Some trend values are lost at both ends of the series.
(C) It gives an equation that can be used directly for forecasting.
(D) A five-yearly moving average is placed against the middle year of each group.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: An even period falls between years, so (A) holds. With a period of \(k\), no average is available for the first and last few years, so (B) holds. An odd period has a middle year, so (D) holds.
Why not the others: (C) is false: moving averages give no equation; the least squares method does. Options (C) and (D) include (C); (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: Use least squares when a forecast is needed.

questions.sub_topic: Values of 4x + 6y on a five-cornered region
questions.question:
The corner points of a feasible region are \((0, 2)\), \((3, 0)\), \((6, 0)\), \((6, 8)\) and \((0, 5)\). For \(Z = 4x + 6y\), match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) The maximum value of \(Z\)
(B) The minimum value of \(Z\)
(C) The value of \(Z\) at \((6, 0)\)
(D) Where the minimum is attained

List-II
(I) \(12\)
(II) \(24\)
(III) Every point of the segment joining \((0, 2)\) and \((3, 0)\)
(IV) \(72\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Step 1: \(Z = 12, 12, 24, 72, 30\) at the five corners
Step 2: Maximum \(72\) at \((6, 8)\) (IV); minimum \(12\) (I)
Step 3: \(Z(6, 0) = 24\) (II)
Step 4: The minimum is reached at two adjacent corners, so at every point of the edge between them (III)
Common mistake: Naming only one corner for (D); \(Z = 2(2x + 3y)\) is constant along the edge \(2x + 3y = 6\).
Key point: Two adjacent optimal corners make the whole edge optimal.

questions.sub_topic: Marginal cost of a cubic cost function at x = 3
questions.question: The total cost of producing \(x\) units is \(C(x) = 0.005x^3 - 0.02x^2 + 30x + 5000\). The marginal cost when \(x = 3\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹30.015
Given: \(MC = \dfrac{dC}{dx} = 0.015x^2 - 0.04x + 30\)
Formula: substitute \(x = 3\)
Step 1: \(0.015 \times 9 = 0.135\); \(0.04 \times 3 = 0.12\)
Step 2: \(MC = 0.135 - 0.12 + 30 = 30.015\)
Common mistake: (A) drops the \(-0.04x\) term. (B) keeps only the constant 30.
Key point: The fixed cost 5000 does not affect marginal cost.

questions.sub_topic: Facts about one symmetric 2 × 2 matrix — which claims fail
questions.question:
For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}\), consider the following statements:
(A) \(|A| = 1\)
(B) \(A\) is symmetric.
(C) \(A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\)
(D) \(A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}5&3\\3&2\end{bmatrix}\)
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C) only
Why: \(|A| = 2 - 1 = 1\), \(A^T = A\), and \(A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}4 + 1&2 + 1\\2 + 1&1 + 1\end{bmatrix}\), so (A), (B), (D) hold. Only (C) is false: \(A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}\).
Why not the others: Options (A), (B) and (C) name a true statement as false.
Key point: For a 2 × 2 inverse, swap the diagonal and change the signs of the other two entries.

questions.sub_topic: Second five-yearly moving average
questions.question: For the values 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 over six years, the second five-yearly moving average is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(10\)
Given: the second group is the 2nd to 6th values
Formula: average of five consecutive values
Step 1: \(\dfrac{6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14}{5} = \dfrac{50}{5} = 10\)
Common mistake: \(8\) (B) is the first five-yearly average.
Key point: Each new average drops the oldest value and adds the next.

questions.sub_topic: Separable equation y′ = y² through (0, 1)
questions.question: The solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^2\) with \(y(0) = 1\) gives \(y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\) equal to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(2\)
Given: \(\dfrac{dy}{y^2} = dx\)
Formula: \(-\dfrac{1}{y} = x + C\)
Step 1: \(y(0) = 1\): \(C = -1\), so \(y = \dfrac{1}{1 - x}\)
Step 2: \(y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{1/2} = 2\)
Common mistake: \(e^{1/2}\) (C) solves \(y' = y\) instead. \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) (B) drops the minus sign.
Key point: \(\int y^{-2}\,dy = -y^{-1}\).

questions.sub_topic: Quantities in a one-sample t-test with n = 25
questions.question:
A sample of 25 has mean 52 and standard deviation 5 (divisor \(n - 1\)). \(H_0: \mu = 50\) is tested. Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Degrees of freedom
(B) Standard error of the mean
(C) The \(t\)-statistic
(D) The sample variance

List-II
(I) \(25\)
(II) \(2\)
(III) \(24\)
(IV) \(1\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Step 1: df \(= n - 1 = 24\) (III)
Step 2: SE \(= \dfrac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \dfrac{5}{5} = 1\) (IV)
Step 3: \(t = \dfrac{52 - 50}{1} = 2\) (II)
Step 4: \(s^2 = 25\) (I)
Common mistake: Taking df as 25, the sample size, which is also the variance here.
Key point: Standard error \(= \dfrac{s}{\sqrt{n}}\).

questions.sub_topic: A² − 2A for a symmetric matrix
questions.question: For \(A = \begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}\), \(A^2 - 2A\) equals:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(3I\)
Given: \(A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}1 + 4&2 + 2\\2 + 2&4 + 1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}5&4\\4&5\end{bmatrix}\)
Formula: \(2A = \begin{bmatrix}2&4\\4&2\end{bmatrix}\)
Step 1: \(A^2 - 2A = \begin{bmatrix}3&0\\0&3\end{bmatrix} = 3I\)
Common mistake: (D) subtracts \(A^2\) from \(2A\).
Key point: Multiply row by column before subtracting.

questions.sub_topic: Value of a 2 × 2 determinant with a negative entry
questions.question: The value of \(\begin{vmatrix}4&-2\\3&1\end{vmatrix}\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) \(10\)
Given: \(a = 4\), \(b = -2\), \(c = 3\), \(d = 1\)
Formula: \(ad - bc\)
Step 1: \(4 - (-6) = 10\)
Common mistake: \(-2\) (B) computes \(4 - 6\), losing the sign of \(b\).
Key point: Subtracting a negative product adds it.

questions.sub_topic: Price of a bond with half-yearly coupons
questions.question: A bond of face value ₹1,000 pays an 8% coupon per annum in half-yearly instalments and is redeemed at par after 2 years. If the yield is 10% per annum compounded half-yearly, the price of the bond is about (\((1.05)^{-4} = 0.8227\)):
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) ₹964.54
Given: coupon ₹40 every half-year, \(i = 0.05\), \(n = 4\)
Formula: \(V = C \cdot \dfrac{1 - (1 + i)^{-n}}{i} + F(1 + i)^{-n}\)
Step 1: \(40 \times \dfrac{1 - 0.8227}{0.05} = 40 \times 3.546 = 141.84\)
Step 2: \(1000 \times 0.8227 = 822.70\); \(V \approx 964.54\)
Common mistake: ₹965.29 (B) uses yearly coupons of ₹80 at 10%. ₹1,036.30 (D) swaps the coupon and yield rates.
Key point: Halve both the coupon and the rate, and double the number of periods.

questions.sub_topic: Means, variances and standard deviations
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Mean of a binomial distribution with \(n = 10\), \(p = 0.2\)
(B) Variance of the same binomial distribution
(C) Standard deviation of a Poisson distribution with mean 9
(D) Mean of a Poisson distribution with \(P(X = 0) = e^{-4}\)

List-II
(I) \(1.6\)
(II) \(2\)
(III) \(4\)
(IV) \(3\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Step 1: \(np = 10 \times 0.2 = 2\) (II)
Step 2: \(npq = 2 \times 0.8 = 1.6\) (I)
Step 3: Poisson variance = mean = 9, so SD \(= 3\) (IV)
Step 4: \(P(X = 0) = e^{-\lambda} = e^{-4}\), so \(\lambda = 4\) (III)
Common mistake: Taking the SD in (C) as 9; for a Poisson distribution the variance, not the SD, equals the mean.
Key point: Poisson: \(P(X = 0) = e^{-\lambda}\).

questions.sub_topic: Minimum of 5x + 7y on an unbounded region
questions.question: The minimum value of \(Z = 5x + 7y\) subject to \(2x + y \ge 8\), \(x + 2y \ge 10\), \(x, y \ge 0\) is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) \(38\)
Given: corners \((0, 8)\), \((2, 4)\), \((10, 0)\)
Formula: evaluate \(Z\), then check the unbounded region
Step 1: \(Z = 56, 38, 50\)
Step 2: \(5x + 7y < 38\) has no point in the region, so the minimum is 38, at \((2, 4)\)
Common mistake: \(50\) (A) skips the corner where the two lines meet.
Key point: On an unbounded region, confirm the minimum with the half-plane \(Z < 38\).

questions.topic: Unit I: Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications
questions.sub_topic: Three workers from their pairwise times
questions.question: A and B together finish a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. All three together finish it in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) \(10\) days
Given: one day's work of the pairs: \(\dfrac{1}{12}, \dfrac{1}{15}, \dfrac{1}{20}\)
Formula: \(2(a + b + c) = \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{5 + 4 + 3}{60} = \dfrac{1}{5}\)
Step 1: \(a + b + c = \dfrac{1}{10}\)
Step 2: All three take 10 days
Common mistake: \(5\) (A) forgets that each worker is counted twice in the sum.
Key point: Adding the three pairs counts everyone twice.

questions.sub_topic: Minimum average cost of a cubic cost function
questions.question: The total cost of producing \(x\) units is \(C(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 15x\). The minimum average cost is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) \(6\)
Given: \(AC = \dfrac{C(x)}{x} = x^2 - 6x + 15\)
Formula: \(\dfrac{d(AC)}{dx} = 2x - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 3\); second derivative \(2 > 0\)
Step 1: \(AC(3) = 9 - 18 + 15 = 6\)
Common mistake: \(3\) (A) is the output, not the cost. \(18\) (C) is the total cost \(C(3)\).
Key point: Minimise \(\dfrac{C}{x}\), not \(C\).
